To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the incidence of loss of heterozygosity on chromosome 11p was not increased in hepatocellular carcinoma; 2) the loss of heterozyosity on chromosome 3p was not significantly different between HBV‐positive and HBV‐negative patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.

(1) loss of 11p13 alleles was not detected in HBV negative HCCs; (2) loss of 9p21 alleles was detected in HBV positive HCCs, but was not detected in HCCs of HBV negative individuals; (3) loss of 17p13.1 alleles was detected in HCC of HBV positive patients, and was also detected in HCC from HBV negative individuals.
the loss of alleles at the chromosome arm (11p) was not observed in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) of patients who were negative for hepatitis B virus (HVB).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of hepatocellular carcinoma, the third most frequent cause of cancer‐related death in the world.
the study of the genetic alterations in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in patients without HBV infection.
a possible role of the chromosome arm 17q in human hepatocarcinomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present data do not support a role of the 11p locus in the genesis of HBV negative HCC.
no evidence for loss of DNA sequences on 11p is available for HCCs of HBV negative individuals.
loss of 11p is not a frequent mechanism in HBV negative HCCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loss of 11p13 alleles in HCC of HBV negative individuals does not occur.
no loss of DNA sequences from 11p was detected in HBV negative HCCs, and that the 3p loss was not a general phenomenon of HCCs, although 2 out of 8 cases showed 3p deletion.
loss of heterozygosity at 11p is not a frequent event in HBV negative HCCs, and that other genetic mechanisms, such as point mutations, may be more important for the pathogenesis of these tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now use this method to study the effect of the 11p13 gene on the 11p14 gene.
loss of heterozygosity on 11p does not seem to play a major role in hepatocarcino­genesis in HBV‐negative patients.
we have developed a method for measuring the loss of genetic material at the chromosome 11p locus, and we have shown that this method can be used to detect genetic loss in hepatocellular carcinoma.
